metadata.title: Polarized light and geometric phase in qg units: Stokes parameters, Mueller matrices and Stokes' theorem

creators.name: Monteverde, Vicente Humberto
creators.affiliation: Universidad del Museo Social Argentino (UMSA), Argentina

metadata.description: The qang project describes qubits by measurement-level quantities, the qg values qg_P=⟨ P⟩. This short note states two classical results in those units, implemented and checked in the qang library (pip install qang, version 0.6.0). First, a polarization state of light is a qubit: the normalized Stokes parameters are exactly the qg values, the degree of polarization is the length of the qg vector, and a lossless Mueller matrix is the qg gate rule qg'_P=qg_(U^† PU). Malus's law becomes I=I_0(1+qg_Zcos2θ+qg_Xsin2θ)/2 for any input state. Second, the geometric phase of a closed loop on the Bloch (Poincaré) sphere is minus half the enclosed solid angle, which is Stokes' theorem for the Berry curvature. For a loop at constant qg_Z the phase is (qg_Z-1)/2 of a turn: it is fixed by qg_Z alone. Nothing here is new physics. The contribution is the translation into qang's units and a set of 26 numerical checks, with the phase computed three independent ways.
metadata.notes: Every numerical claim is reproduced by the open-source library qang (pip install qang, version 0.6.16) and pinned by its tests; predictions were committed before each run.
